public_rationale: Marcus explicitly expresses uncertainty. Scoring that sentence would require choosing what 'this' refers to and turning 'we don’t know' into a defined claim about public knowledge. Neither choice is supplied by his words. Scoring both outages separately would also add commitments he did not make. The sentence therefore lacks a sufficiently definite proposition for a fair supported-or-contradicted assessment. This conclusion concerns the wording, not the actual causes of either outage.
limitations: No external evidence was sought because incident findings would not settle the ambiguity in the claim itself.
This assessment does not evaluate the accuracy of the earlier warnings or any broader causal insinuation in the post.

our_interpretation: The sentence expresses uncertainty about a cause; it does not affirm either proposed cause or explicitly make the alternatives exhaustive.
The supplied context leaves 'this' ambiguous between the FAA ground stop and the Microsoft outage.
The sentence does not define whose knowledge 'we' describes. Treating it as a claim about all publicly available information would add a criterion the speaker did not supply.
The dates identify earlier warnings, not a forecast deadline or the period of the outage.
criteria.support_condition: No unambiguous support condition can be set for the sentence as written. Testing the expressed uncertainty would first require identifying the incident and whose knowledge is being described.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No unambiguous contradiction condition can be set without those clarifications. An official finding about one incident would not by itself contradict this sentence with its referent and knowledge scope unspecified.
